package.author: Han Lin
package.description: Flip the Windows default audio output between two devices in milliseconds.

en-US.author: Han Lin
en-US.description: Flip the Windows default audio output between two devices in milliseconds.
en-US.longDescription:
Toggle Audio switches the Windows default playback device between two outputs you choose
(for example monitor speakers and a Bluetooth headphone transmitter), then exits. It is a
native x64 executable with no runtime dependencies and no background process, made to sit
behind a macro key in Logitech G HUB, Stream Deck, AutoHotkey or a Windows shortcut.
A full toggle takes about 40 ms. It includes a small settings dialog to pick the two devices,
a command line (list, get, set) with documented exit codes, and a console-free launcher
executable for hotkeys.
en-US.name: Toggle Audio
en-US.releaseNotes:
Initial native release: instant default-playback toggle with unplugged-device fallback,
list/get/set command line, settings dialog, two executables (console and console-free),
per-user JSON configuration, MSI installer with Start Menu entry and optional PATH, and
reproducible benchmarks in C, Rust, C#, Go, Zig and PowerShell.
